title: Koru decoy template, schema v1
description: Koru decoy and breadcrumb template (ADR-0004). Templates are packages/decoys/*.toml files; the TOML document corresponds one-to-one to this schema's JSON data model. Rust counterpart: koru_decoy::Template (deny_unknown_fields). A template contains only placeholders: the {{name}}, {{name.sub}}, {{template:name}}, {{template:path}}, and {{file_time.sub}} placeholders and the |lower, |upper filters in the content and path texts are filled at install time with CSPRNG-generated values. The cross-field rules (placeholders being defined, no '..', '.', or empty components in the target path, no 'koru' substring, a secret file being 0600, no fixed secrets in a template, no command field in an MCP decoy) and the generated content's format and safety checks live not in this schema but in koru_decoy::Template::validate and package validation (koru decoy validate).

id.description: The template's unique id within the package; used in cross-references ({{template:name}}). It cannot contain the 'koru' substring.

description.description: What the template is (in English). It does not enter the installed content.

kind.description: decoy: a file carrying a fake credential or secret value. breadcrumb: a record pointing at fake targets (~/.bash_history, ~/.ssh/config, known_hosts). The detection layer treats the two as separate signals.

class.description: A free class tag (e.g. ssh_key, cloud_credentials, mcp_config). Writing a new tag is enough for a new decoy kind.

format.description: The format of the generated content; at validation, the content is parsed in this format and safety rules are applied.

secret.description: Does the file carry a secret value (key, password, token)? If true, target.mode must be 0o600.

content.description: Content with placeholders. If placement is 'append', the block to append to the end of the existing file, and it must end with a newline.

values.description: Value generators; the key is the value name (starts with a lowercase letter; path, file_time, and index are reserved).

path.description: A path relative to the root directory (the target user's home directory) or an absolute path under a root allowed at install time. It cannot contain '..', '.', an empty component, or a backslash. It may refer to simple values via placeholders (e.g. a dated file name).

mode.description: The file mode (written in octal in TOML, e.g. 0o600). No execute bit, no write bit for group or others; the owner must be able to read.

placement.description: new_file: if the target exists, the install is refused (nothing is overwritten). append: appended to the end of the existing file; a backup is taken first, and on removal only the appended lines are removed. Only for line-based formats.

time_range.description: The range for the file's natural modification time (days back from now); the time is chosen weighted toward working hours and weekdays. Usable in content, e.g. {{file_time.date}}.

value.description: A value generator; the 'kind' field selects the kind.

inner_value.description: A value generator inside a repeat (repeats cannot nest).

random.description: A random string from an alphabet; an optional fixed prefix and suffix (e.g. base32 with the AKIA prefix).

choice.description: A random choice from a list (name, host name, profile name). Choices cannot contain double quotes, backslashes, or placeholders.

number.description: A random integer in the range (both ends inclusive).

bcrypt.description: A random value shaped like a bcrypt password hash ($2b$<cost>$...); it is not the hash of a real password.

github_token.description: A value shaped like a GitHub personal access token (ghp_ + 30 characters + a CRC32 checksum); it belongs to no account.

ssh_ed25519.description: A freshly generated ed25519 key pair; authorized nowhere. Sub-fields: private (the OpenSSH private key file), public (ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment), public_key (without comment).

test_net_ipv4.description: An IPv4 address from the RFC 5737 documentation networks (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24); unroutable. The placeholder target of breadcrumbs until the isolated trap VM on the roadmap.

timestamp.description: A natural time in the past. Sub-fields: date, time, datetime, iso, unix, year.

repeat.description: A random number of repeats of the inner template (e.g. SQL rows); inner values are regenerated per repeat. The inner template may refer to inner values, {{index}}, and the template's own values.
